## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world diagnostic skills for latency issues caused by CPU power management using only native Linux interfaces.

## Key Concepts

- CPU frequency scaling and intel_pstate
- Idle/C-states and turbo behavior
- Observability with native /proc/.sys tooling
- Safe thread pinning and governor changes

## Code Example

```bash
mpstat -P ALL 1 2
for c in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq; do echo "CPU=${c##*/}: $(cat $c)"; done
grep -H . /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state*/name
taskset -c 0-1 -p <pid>
for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you verify the result across heterogeneous CPUs?
- What risks exist when pinning threads on a busy core?
